title: Identifying Causal Effects When Interventions Mistarget through a Known Realization Channel
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4; the full-table iff is sound, but no channel-specific SCM-compatible survivor theory or higher-dimensional unknown-DAG boundary is delivered.
gap_reasons: The note does not deliver a new structural characterization of which SCM-compatible causal queries survive singular channels: the constrained-face theorem ignores cross-row SCM compatibility, while the exact compatible criterion is generic response-function linear programming already attributed to prior work.
The known-DAG recovery result and two-node Markovian contrast do not resolve the advertised unknown-DAG boundary beyond that base case.

The projected score is constrained by this limited practical reach, the lack of a channel-specific survivor theory, and the absence of computations or applications demonstrating that the generic fiber criterion yields usable conclusions.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact full-intervention-table identification iff for known product mistargeting channels over arbitrary finite pointed alphabets and unrestricted recursive SCMs, with necessity witnessed by strictly positive binary common-SCM pairs. It also derived constrained-face and closed-response-fiber criteria, known-DAG recovery, and two-node Markovian contrasts. The field-level promise collapsed because the compatible criterion remained the generic response-function LP: a channel-specific survivor quotient, the n>=3 unknown-DAG boundary, and a sampling/robustness layer remain open.
tldr: When attempted fixed-zero interventions pass through a known nodewise Boolean realization channel, the complete causal table over arbitrary finite endogenous state spaces is identified for every recursive SCM with arbitrary latent dependence exactly when every channel contrast is nonzero. No observational-positivity or finite-exogenous-support restriction is needed. Necessity is causal, not merely linear algebra: it is witnessed by two strictly positive finite binary common SCMs with the same complete noisy family and different fixed-zero effects, embedded into larger alphabets when necessary. In the singular case, the binary ambient result is a constrained-face row-space criterion, while unrestricted SCM-compatible queries have exact attained bounds over closed finite response fibers. No channel-specific quotient of common-SCM response types beyond removal of repeated observation coordinates has been derived.
gap: Stochastic off-target actions have been formalized, but the closest discovery work observes the realized target. Mixture-identification results either assume a known causal Bayesian network and exclusion or impose linear-Gaussian causal sufficiency. The literature inspected does not give an iff for a complete known latent-target channel over positive nonparametric common SCMs. Generic response-function optimization can decide survivor queries, but it does not by itself explain the channel's exact causal information frontier.
fill: Establish the tensor algebra and the sound-and-complete coefficient quotient on the constrained fixed-zero face; prove the multivariate positive-common-SCM iff with named-effect witnesses lying in that face's collapsed kernel for every singular-rate stratum; characterize survivor queries by exact SCM fibers without claiming generic LP novelty; and delimit the conclusion through the one-node, known-DAG Markovian, and two-node unknown-DAG Markovian regimes. A further contribution is pursued only if the Boolean channel admits compression beyond Rossetto--Antonucci's generic quotient.
